population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
note: Regorafenib, lenvatinib, anlotinib (catequentinib) and famitinib all showed RCC activity in patients; only regorafenib's 786-O xenografts predicted it prospectively, the lenvatinib and anlotinib mouse data came after the trials, and no famitinib RCC model was found.
label: RCC (VEGFR multikinase TKIs)

engagement.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is first publication; the rat work predates the first-in-man study, whose start date was not retrieved.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry dated at first publication. The rat tumour is a glioma, not RCC; it is the PD system the class member was carried on.
engagement.note: One oral regorafenib dose cut Gadomer extravasation in rat GS9L tumours, correlating with growth inhibition; no human perfusion data yet.
engagement.short: Rat tumour perfusion falls on regorafenib
engagement.quote: Regorafenib administered once orally at 10 mg/kg significantly decreased the extravasation of Gadomer in the vasculature of rat GS9L glioblastoma tumor xenografts.

engagement.magnitude_basis: DCE-MRI tumour perfusion change, rat vs patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the magnitude of the Ktrans change and how many RCC patients were imaged were not read.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (the phase 1 paper does not show the rat data). Mixed solid-tumour phase 1 accepted for engagement; perfusion is downstream of VEGFR blockade.
engagement.note: First-in-man regorafenib study: DCE-MRI tumour perfusion and plasma cytokines moved, as the rat perfusion readout predicted.
engagement.short: Patient tumour perfusion fell on DCE-MRI
engagement.quote: Tumor perfusion and plasma cytokine analysis showed biologic activity of regorafenib.
engagement.reason: Patient perfusion fell as rats predicted

dose.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the FDA clinical pharmacology reviews (NDA 203085, 206947) were grepped for an efficacious exposure from xenografts and none was found. Human doses came from phase 1 MTD.
dose.judgement: Doses for regorafenib (160 mg) and lenvatinib (24 mg; 18 mg with everolimus) were set by phase 1 tolerability, which is not a model target.
dose.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
dose.note: Xenograft and rat work for regorafenib and lenvatinib gave dose-response in mg/kg but no stated human exposure target or margin in sources read.
dose.quote: Regorafenib exhibited potent dose-dependent TGI in various preclinical human xenograft models in mice, with tumor shrinkages observed in breast MDA-MB-231 and renal 786-O carcinoma models.

efficacy.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The RCC phase 2 (NCT00664326) started April 2008, so the xenograft data likely predate it; dated at publication.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first public date of the model data.
efficacy.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
efficacy.note: Regorafenib shrank 786-O renal carcinoma xenografts; the first-line RCC phase 2 had not reported.
efficacy.quote: Regorafenib exhibited potent dose-dependent TGI in various preclinical human xenograft models in mice, with tumor shrinkages observed in breast MDA-MB-231 and renal 786-O carcinoma models.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour shrinkage vs objective response rate
efficacy.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry NCT00664326 results first posted 2012-11-28; paper online 2012-09-06.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; uncontrolled phase 2 with an ORR primary read as the class working. Regorafenib was not developed further in RCC; that business decision is not scored. Study 205 (lenvatinib) moved to the lenvatinib track of this model (entry 3).
efficacy.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2 of first-line regorafenib: 39.6% objective response (primary endpoint), as tumour shrinkage in 786-O xenografts predicted. Single-arm trial with no preset success bar: scored on its primary endpoint (ORR 39.6%) in the direction the model predicted.
efficacy.quote: 19 patients (39·6%, 90% CI 27·7-52·5) had an objective response, all of which were partial responses.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: combination vs monotherapy ordering: xenograft growth vs PFS
efficacy.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMC5406533 available, not read in full). Whether the xenografts were run before Study 205 read out (2014-15) is not stated in the abstract. Year from the Lenvima label revised 05/2016 (206947s003lbl.pdf), section 12.1, earlier than Matsuki 2017.
efficacy.judgement: Kept on the same RCC-xenograft track (same system, different cell lines). Scored retro because the paper opens from the known phase 2 result and investigates mechanism.
efficacy.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
efficacy.note: Eisai's A-498, Caki-1 and Caki-2 xenografts, published after Study 205, reproduced lenvatinib (with everolimus) beating either drug alone. Combination trial (lenvatinib plus everolimus), scored on Study 205's PFS primary. Dated 2016: the May 2016 Lenvima label first stated the xenograft result beside Study 205.
efficacy.quote: Lenvatinib plus everolimus showed greater antitumor activity than either monotherapy in three human RCC xenograft mouse models (A-498, Caki-1, and Caki-2).

patient_trials.quote: Single-agent lenvatinib significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with everolimus alone (HR 0·61, 95% CI 0·38-0·98; p=0·048).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth inhibition vs PFS comparable to sunitinib
efficacy.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Patient side Zhou 2019 (NCT02072031, no registry results posted): PFS 17.5 vs 16.6 months vs sunitinib.
efficacy.judgement: Comparison stated in one source (abstract opens with the patient efficacy, then the mouse result). Catequentinib is read as anlotinib. Primary objective is a biomarker search; the growth inhibition is what reproduces the clinic.
efficacy.note: Anlotinib inhibited Renca tumours 39-52% in mice, run after the phase 2 had shown anlotinib comparable to sunitinib. Catequentinib read as anlotinib (AL3818); first-line randomised phase 2 versus sunitinib, PFS primary.
efficacy.quote: The tumor growth inhibition rates of ANL were 39% and 52% at low (3 mg/kg) and high (6 mg/kg) dose levels, without obvious toxicity.
efficacy.reason: Retro only; no prospective RCC model

patient_trials.quote: The median PFS was similar with anlotinib and sunitinib (17.5 vs. 16.6 months, p > .05).

efficacy.model: Lenvatinib 19-model human xenograft panel with vascular score (MVD + pericyte coverage) biomarker
efficacy.note: Xenograft panel tied lenvatinib tumour shrinkage to high vascular score; kidney cancer had the highest MVD among human tumours, suggesting high-MVD tumours respond.
efficacy.short: High vascular score marks lenvatinib responders
efficacy.quote: MVD and pericyte-coverage of tumor vasculature might be biomarkers and suggest cases that would respond for lenvatinib therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the panel's publication; a patient-selection prediction, so prediction_level patient.

efficacy.model: Lenvatinib 19-model human xenograft panel with vascular score (MVD + pericyte coverage) biomarker
efficacy.note: In CLEAR, angiogenesis and microvessel-density gene signatures did not track PFS on lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab, though they did on sunitinib. Combination regimen (lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab); a biomarker analysis, not the trial's primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: MVD signature did not predict lenvatinib benefit
efficacy.quote: No associations between PFS and gene signature scores were observed for L + P. With sunitinib, high proliferation and MYC signature scores showed shorter PFS; high angiogenesis and microvessel density signature scores showed longer PFS.
efficacy.reason: MVD signature not linked to PFS
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Patient readout is an RNA microvessel-density signature, not IHC vascular score, and the regimen adds pembrolizumab; the lenvatinib+everolimus arm's biomarkers are not in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Paired the xenograft vascular-score prediction with CLEAR's prespecified biomarker analysis; a null association in the lenvatinib arm scored contra rather than unsettled because the regimen contains a member drug.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (CT26, Hepa1-6, LL/2) treated with lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1
efficacy.note: Lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 beat either agent alone in immunocompetent mouse tumours, published after lenvatinib-pembrolizumab RCC activity was reported. Opened at 2018: the same Eisai Hepa1-6 lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 system was first published by Kimura 2018.
efficacy.quote: Antitumor activity of lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1 was greater than that of either single treatment.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; models are non-RCC syngeneic tumours. Earliest use Kimura 2018 Cancer Sci (doi:10.1111/cas.13806, online 2018-11-16), per checker; Kato 2019 kept as the quoted source.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry (existence only); the scored entry is a retrodiction because the combination's RCC activity was public (phase 1b, KEYNOTE-146) before this paper.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (CT26, Hepa1-6, LL/2) treated with lenvatinib plus anti-PD-1
efficacy.note: CLEAR: lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab lengthened PFS over sunitinib, consistent with the mouse combination benefit already seen in RCC patients. Combination trial (lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab versus sunitinib), scored on PFS primary.
efficacy.quote: Progression-free survival was longer with lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab than with sunitinib (median, 23.9 vs. 9.2 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.32 to 0.49; P<0.001)
efficacy.reason: Mouse combo data came after patient signal
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. CLEAR compares with sunitinib, not lenvatinib alone, so the model's combination-over-monotherapy claim is matched in direction only.
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: CLEAR's own background states the combination already had RCC activity before Kato 2019.

efficacy.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
efficacy.confidence_note: Label text checked by the checker (206947s003, section 12.1); the quoted sentence is verbatim from Matsuki 2017. The lenvatinib result was already known from Study 205, so no prospective prediction exists.
efficacy.judgement: Track split: the system was used for regorafenib (2011) and lenvatinib; the lenvatinib track opens at its first public use, dated by the Lenvima label revised 05/2016 (section 12.1), which states the same xenograft result.
efficacy.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
efficacy.note: Opening entry for lenvatinib on the RCC cell-line xenograft system: first public use for lenvatinib (label 2016, Matsuki 2017).
efficacy.short: RCC xenografts first run for lenvatinib
efficacy.quote: Lenvatinib plus everolimus showed greater antitumor activity than either monotherapy in three human RCC xenograft mouse models (A-498, Caki-1, and Caki-2).

safety.magnitude_basis: liver injury, rats/dogs vs RCC patients (1/49 serious hepatic event; no liver-enzyme AE at the 5% reporting threshold)
safety.population: Previously untreated metastatic or unresectable clear-cell RCC (NCT00664326, n=49)
safety.confidence_note: Registry results table (serious events: 'Hepatic function abnormal', 1/49; other events reported at a 5% threshold list no ALT/AST rise). Eisen 2012 full text not read. Model side read in FDA pharmacology review (bundle).
safety.judgement: Imported-harm ruling: RCC patients were measured (NCT00664326), so their result sets the status instead of the colorectal registration. One serious hepatic event in 49 matches in direction; scored same, partial.
safety.note: Rats and dogs showed liver injury; in the RCC phase 2, one of 49 patients had serious abnormal hepatic function. RCC patients now decide, replacing the colorectal import.
safety.short: Animal liver injury seen rarely in RCC

safety.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the trial; model side read in FDA pharmacology review NDA 206947 (thyroid filing, 2015).
safety.judgement: Paired by me: FDA review ('Lenvatinib induced renal toxicity in rats and monkeys, including proteinuria') against the RCC trial. Quote truncated at 40 words. Model first use is a proxy (Study 205 registered 2010).
safety.note: Rats and monkeys developed proteinuria and glomerulopathy; in Study 205, proteinuria was lenvatinib's commonest grade 3-4 event (19%).
safety.short: Animal proteinuria seen in RCC patients
safety.quote: The most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-emergent adverse event in patients allocated lenvatinib plus everolimus was diarrhoea (ten [20%]), in those assigned single-agent lenvatinib it was proteinuria (ten [19%])
safety.reason: Animal kidney and liver harms recurred

safety.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
safety.population: Unselected (advanced or metastatic RCC, mostly clear-cell)
safety.quote: These data demonstrate that regorafenib is a well-tolerated, orally active multikinase inhibitor with a distinct target profile that may have therapeutic benefit in human malignancies.
safety.note: Passing tolerability claim in the xenograft efficacy paper, scored as a safety prediction: regorafenib well tolerated at effective doses.
safety.judgement: Passing-tolerability ruling: the efficacy paper's 'well-tolerated' statement is the model's safety prediction.

safety.magnitude_basis: tolerability at the effective dose: 'well tolerated' in mice vs common grade 3 drug-related events in patients
safety.model: Human xenografts in nude mice (786-O renal and others)
safety.population: Previously untreated metastatic or unresectable clear-cell RCC (NCT00664326)
safety.quote: Grade 3 drug-related adverse events were common, most frequently hand and foot skin reaction (16 patients, 33%), diarrhoea (five patients, 10%), renal failure (five patients, 10%), fatigue (four patients, 8%), and hypertension (three patients, 6%).
safety.note: RCC patients on 160 mg regorafenib had common grade 3 toxicity, 35% drug-related serious events and two likely drug-related deaths; the authors call for close monitoring.
safety.short: Not well tolerated in RCC patients
safety.reason: Tolerability claim failed in RCC patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Whether regorafenib phase 1 congress abstracts predate April 2011 (which would make this a retrodiction) was not checked; the status is contra either way.
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Wilhelm 2011's 'well-tolerated' against Eisen 2012, whose authors conclude 'the drug's safety profile requires close monitoring'. Mice can show tolerability limits, so this is a scored miss.

safety.magnitude_basis: tolerability: 'without obvious toxicity' in mice vs grade 3-4 AEs 28.9% (fewer than sunitinib) in patients
safety.quote: The clinical efficacy of anlotinib was similar to that of sunitinib as the first-line treatment for mRCC, but with a more favorable safety profile.
safety.note: Passing tolerability claim ('without obvious toxicity', Renca mice, 2022) scored as safety; anlotinib's own RCC patients had already shown a favourable profile, so a retrodiction.
safety.short: Renca tolerability matches known patient profile
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Patients still had 28.9% grade 3-4 AEs, so the match is partial. Catequentinib read as anlotinib (AL3818).
safety.judgement: Passing-tolerability ruling plus the dose/safety retrodiction rule: anlotinib's own patient safety (Zhou 2019, ASCO 2016) predates Du 2022, so retro.
